Checked on **2026-11-21** (UTC) against the [OSV](https://osv.dev) database, by `kb-vuln-scan/1`. The scan asks about
the commit of each pinned component, so a release candidate and a moved tag are judged by the code that is pinned. A
weekly workflow repeats it, rebuilds this page and the configurator's data, and opens an issue when an advisory
appears; it commits nothing. If the data is more than 10 days old the configurator and this page say so.

**0 open, 8 reviewed** of 8 advisories for 1 of the 24 pinned components; **none known** for the others.

An advisory means the database lists the pinned commit as affected. It is not a verdict on whether kb-core or a
product built from it is exposed: read the advisory, then decide, and record the decision in the [SOUP list](soup.md).

A reviewed advisory is one on the reviewed list, `tools/vuln/reviewed.json` (`kb-vex/1`): its primary source, the
upstream advisory, names the exact pinned version as patched, and the entry holds the reason, the source and the date
of the review. It stays in the list, marked *fixed in the pinned version*, and does not count as open. An entry
applies only while the scanned version equals the one it was reviewed for; if the pin moves, the advisory is open
again. See [Known data issues](../configurator.md#known-data-issues).
